previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and prior amputations was admitted for osteomyelitis in the right index finger and right foot, presenting with pain, foul drainage, and fever. Imaging and biopsy confirmed bone infection in both sites. He underwent amputation of the right index finger tip and a transmetatarsal amputation of the right foot. Cultures grew Proteus mirabilis, sensitive to ertapenem. Due to equivocal margins in the foot, he was discharged on a prolonged course of outpatient IV ertapenem via a PICC line. His hypertension was managed with adjustment of labetalol to 600 mg twice daily, and his transplant function remained stable with continued immunosuppression. He was discharged home ambulatory with walker assistance, with plans for weekly lab monitoring and follow-up with podiatry and infectious disease.

complicated by poor wound healing in setting of peripheral 
vascular disease. Has been following with Podiatry as 
outpatient, and has been trying to get in to see Vascular as 
outpatient but could not get appointment. Started on empiric 
vancomycin, ceftriaxone and flagyl. Switched to ciprofloxacin

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  FOOT AP,LAT AND OBL RIGHT

INDICATION:  ___ with right foot infection, evaluate for foreign body.

TECHNIQUE:  Three views of the right foot.

COMPARISON:  Right foot radiographs ___.

FINDINGS: 

The patient is status post transmetatarsal amputation through the right foot. 
There is no evidence of acute fracture or dislocation.  Right foot
degenerative changes are stable, including prominent talonavicular spurring. 
There is a small Achilles enthesophyte.  There is suggestion of soft tissue
swelling and skin thickening about the plantar and distal aspect of the right
foot.  There is no subcutaneous emphysema.  Although assessment is difficult
due to prior amputation, there is no definite evidence of osteolysis.  No new
worrisome focal osseous lesion is seen.  There are extensive vascular
calcifications.  No unexpected radiopaque foreign body is identified.

IMPRESSION: 

Soft tissue swelling/edema and skin thickening about the plantar and distal
aspect of the right foot.  No definite evidence of subcutaneous emphysema or
osteolysis to suggest osteomyelitis.
